headline: Deep learning models operate directly on Hi-C contact matrices across chromatin tasks
label: Hi C Matrix Deep Learning
summary: Recent work applies matrix-native architectures to single-cell subcompartments, TAD boundaries, and 3D contact-map retrieval from Hi-C data.
synthesis: The common thread is the treatment of Hi-C contact matrices as two-dimensional or three-dimensional inputs for task-specific learned representations. scSTEC annotates chromatin subcompartments from individual single-cell Hi-C matrices through direct 2D embedding and chromosome-wise consensus, without imputation or cross-cell information. AxialTAD predicts TAD boundaries with a compact architecture built around an Axial Contrast Module, reporting 76-80% fewer parameters than deepTAD. C-Fetch takes a different route, retrieving 3D chromatin contact-map features by reference-guided search over weakly KL-regularized 3D autoencoder representations. What is new across these is the matrix-native design: per-cell analysis without imputation, parameter compactness, and retrieval in representation space. These remain separate tasks rather than one shared model.
